title: Battle of Lake Trasimene
summary: Spring the ambush on the fogbound shore road and capture both Roman field camps within twenty minutes, before the mist lifts and a cohort escapes the basin.
teaching_goal: A nation stands on its commander. Kill him and the camps go quiet and unclaimed - which, against a twenty-minute clock, is the only version of this battle that finishes in time.
narrative_intent: Flaminius' marching column walks blind into a geographical trap along a mist-filled shore road and is destroyed by converging attacks from the heights, while the lakeside Sepulcher altar remains an optional horror.
historical_context: June 217 BC: Hannibal drew the consul Gaius Flaminius along the narrow northern shore of Lake Trasimene. Morning mist lay thick over the lake road while the hilltops stood clear. Gauls and cavalry waited on the heights by the entrance, Balearic slingers and light troops along the ridge, Africans and Iberians on the hill across the exit. The column, strung out in marching order, had no room to deploy. Flaminius was cut down by an Insubrian horseman, Ducarius; some fifteen thousand Romans died, and six thousand who broke out of the van surrendered to Maharbal the next day. Altered here: the column town, the shore camp and Flaminius' post at the basin watch are the game's, and so is the Sepulcher altar by the lake.

victory_conditions.description: Seize both Roman camps. The ambush is not finished until their flags come down.
Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

defeat_conditions.description: Twenty minutes before the mist lifts. If a cohort clears the basin, Rome learns the shape of the trap.
Your camp falls — the field goes with it.
Every soldier lost is counted by the enemy tonight.
The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
A general alone on a dead field is just the last corpse standing.

optional_objectives.description: Break two of the Roman columns on the shore road.

stages.title: Close the trap on the column town
stages.description: Take the Roman marching town at the western mouth of the lake road.
stages.hint: The road runs east along the lake. Bring the Gauls down off the western heights to shut its mouth, and the column has only one way left to go.

stages.title: Take the shore camp
stages.description: Seize the second camp at the eastern end of the lake.
stages.hint: Nothing on the shore road survives once both ends are held.

stages.title: Kill the Roman commanders
stages.description: Flaminius rides at the basin watch south of the road; the van's tribune holds the sanctuary above the eastern ford. Take them before the column turns on your camp.
stages.hint: Their camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.

actions.text: The Roman column enters the corridor in marching order, blind in the mist. Wait for full commitment.
Strike now. Take Flaminius at the basin watch before the column finds your camp.
The Roman van is cutting east along the shore road. Ride it down before it clears the basin.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Mist on the lake road, and the augurs whine. My horse threw me; a standard would not come out of the ground. Dig it out, I told them. Hannibal burns Etruria and runs ahead of me, and I will have him before my colleague can share the credit.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Fifteen thousand in the shallows, and a consul among them. The praetor will climb the Rostra and say only: we have been beaten in a great battle. Rome elects another consul by market day. That is the trick of us: we are not a man.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The mist lifted a little early for you. The Senate called me reckless; let them call this luck. The lake keeps what it is given, and the thing beneath the altar past the eastern stream is not particular about whose it is.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: You have my marching town. I built it in a fog and never looked back, because a consul of the people does not look back. Keep it. The column will be through your hills before you have counted the huts.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: The shore camp. That was the way out, and now there is only the lake. Romans are not, on the whole, a swimming people.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The column is on the lake road in order of march, and it does not stop for mist. Close up and push on. Hannibal is ahead of us, not above us.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_veteran_consul
commander_messages.text: Somebody is trying to cut a way out along the shore. Good. Somebody should get home and describe this accurately.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: My men are at your camp. In fog a soldier strikes whatever is nearest, and I mean every one of them to find you nearest.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: Your men are dying too. Every one of them is a Carthaginian I will not have to chase back to Africa.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The African dies in his own fog by his own lake. Tell the Senate it was done by the new man they never wanted for consul.

commander_messages.speaker: roman_legion_organizer
commander_messages.text: The column is nearly gone and the Gauls are on the road. Let the Insubres come for me. I broke them once by the Addua; they will not take a consul alive.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: Lake on their left, hills on their right, mist over both. Gauls on the heights by the entrance, slingers along the ridge. Nobody moves until the whole column is inside.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: Ducarius the Insubrian knew the consul who burned his country, and has paid him for it. The column has lost its head. Take the town before anyone thinks to pick it up.

commander_messages.speaker: carthage_sword_commander
commander_messages.text: That was the van's road home. Maharbal will collect whoever is still walking in the morning.

theme: Legions march in column through the shoreline corridor — and the hills swallow them whole.
